chapters.1.summary: Moses speaks to all Israel east of the Jordan in the fortieth year. He recalls how the LORD told them at Horeb to go and take the land. He recalls choosing leaders and judges to share his load. At Kadesh the people asked for spies, who brought back good fruit. Still the people refused to go up and said the LORD hated them. The LORD swore that generation would not see the land, except Caleb and Joshua. Moses says the LORD was angry with him too. The people then went up without the LORD and were beaten back.
chapters.1.lds: Moses tells the children what their parents did at Kadesh. What does he say about himself in verse 37?
chapters.2.summary: Israel wandered around Mount Seir for many days. The LORD told them not to fight Esau’s people and to pay for food. He gave Moab and Ammon to Lot’s children, so Israel must leave them alone. Other peoples had also replaced earlier peoples in those lands. Thirty-eight years passed until the fighting men of the first generation died. Then the LORD gave Sihon the Amorite into Israel’s hand. Moses sent Sihon words of peace, and Sihon refused. Israel defeated him and destroyed his cities.
chapters.2.lds: Why must Israel leave some neighboring lands alone? What reason does verse 5 give about Mount Seir?
chapters.3.summary: Og king of Bashan comes out to fight, and the LORD gives him to Israel. Israel takes his sixty walled cities. Moses gives the land east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. Their fighting men must still cross and help their brothers. Moses tells Joshua not to fear the kingdoms ahead. Moses begs the LORD to let him cross and see the good land. The LORD refuses and tells him to look from the top of Pisgah. He must strengthen Joshua, who will lead the people over.
chapters.3.lds: Moses asks to cross the Jordan, and the LORD says no (verses 25–27). What task is he given in verse 28?
chapters.4.summary: Moses tells Israel to keep the statutes and not add or take away. Other nations will call Israel wise for having such laws and so near a God. They must not forget Horeb, where the mountain burned and they heard a voice. They saw no form, so they must make no image of any creature. They must not worship the sun, moon, or stars. If they make idols, they will be scattered among the nations. Yet if they seek the LORD there with all their heart, they will find him. Moses sets apart three cities of refuge east of the Jordan.
chapters.4.lds: What helps you teach God’s commands with care? At Horeb Israel “saw no kind of form” (verse 15). What did they have in its place (verse 12)?
chapters.5.summary: Moses calls all Israel to hear the statutes. He says the covenant at Horeb was made with those alive today. He repeats the ten commandments. The Sabbath command says servants must rest as well as their masters. Israel must remember it was a servant in Egypt until the LORD brought it out. The LORD wrote the words on two stone tablets. The people were afraid of the fire and asked Moses to listen for them. The LORD approved and wished they would always have such a heart.
chapters.5.lds: Verse 15 gives a reason for the Sabbath. What must Israel remember?
chapters.6.summary: Moses gives the commandments Israel must keep in the land. The LORD is one, and Israel must love him with heart, soul, and might. These words must be on their hearts and taught to their children. They talk of them at home, on the road, at night, and at dawn. They are to tie them on hand and forehead and write them on doorposts. In the land they will have cities, houses, wells, and vineyards they did not make. Then they must not forget the LORD. When a son asks what the laws mean, the parent tells of slavery and rescue.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies love for God and teaching the next generation. Verse 7 names four times to talk of God’s words. What are they?
chapters.7.summary: Moses says the LORD will drive out seven nations greater than Israel. Israel is told to destroy them, make no treaty, and not marry among them. The reason given is that they would turn Israel to other gods. Israel must break their altars and burn their images. The LORD chose Israel, though it was the fewest of all peoples. He chose it because he loves it and keeps his oath to the fathers. If Israel obeys, he will bless its children, crops, and herds. The nations will be driven out little by little.
chapters.7.lds: Read covenant responsibilities beside the harm described in the chapter. Keep ancient commands distinct from present Church conduct. Verse 7 says why God did not choose Israel. What reason does verse 8 give for his choice?
chapters.8.summary: Moses tells Israel to remember the forty years in the wilderness. God humbled them, let them hunger, and fed them with manna. He taught them that people do not live by bread alone. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell. Now he brings them to a land of water, wheat, vines, olives, and metal. When they are full and rich, they must not forget the LORD. They must not say their own power got this wealth. If they forget and serve other gods, they will perish like the nations before them.
chapters.8.lds: The Church lesson asks readers to remember God in comfort as well as hardship. What might a full person say “in your heart” (verse 17)? How does verse 18 answer?
chapters.9.summary: Israel is about to cross the Jordan against nations greater and taller. The LORD will go ahead like a devouring fire. Israel must not say the land is a reward for its righteousness. The nations are driven out for their wickedness and because of God’s oath. Israel is a stubborn people, and Moses tells them to remember it. He recalls the golden calf, the broken tablets, and forty days of prayer. He names Taberah, Massah, Kibroth Hattaavah, and Kadesh. He prayed that God would remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and spare his people.
chapters.9.lds: Moses says three times the land is no reward for goodness (verses 4–6). What does he call Israel in verse 6?
chapters.10.summary: Moses recalls cutting two new tablets and making a wooden ark for them. The LORD wrote the ten commandments again, and Moses put them in the ark. Aaron died, and the tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark. The LORD listened to Moses and did not destroy Israel. Now the LORD asks Israel to fear him, love him, and keep his commands. He owns heaven and earth, yet he set his love on their fathers. He takes no bribes and gives justice to the fatherless and widow. He loves the foreigner, so Israel must love the foreigner too.
chapters.10.lds: Verse 19 tells Israel to love the foreigner. What two reasons do verses 18–19 give?
chapters.11.summary: Moses tells those who saw Egypt and the wilderness to love the LORD. The land ahead is not like Egypt, where they watered fields by foot. It is a land of hills and valleys that drinks rain from the sky. The LORD’s eyes are on it all year. If Israel obeys, he will send early and late rain. If they turn to other gods, he will shut the sky. They must teach these words to their children and write them on their doorposts. Moses sets a blessing and a curse before them, on Gerizim and Ebal.
chapters.11.lds: Egypt’s fields were watered by foot, and Canaan’s by rain (verses 10–11). On whom does a rain-fed land depend?
chapters.12.summary: Israel must destroy the places where the nations served their gods. They must not worship the LORD that way, at every hill and tree. They are to bring offerings and tithes to the one place he will choose. There they eat and rejoice with sons, daughters, servants, and the Levite. They may kill and eat meat in any town, as they would a deer. But they must pour out the blood and not eat it. Holy gifts and vows still go to the chosen place. They must not copy the nations, who even burn their children for their gods.
chapters.12.lds: Keep the text’s unnamed sanctuary distinct from a later identification. Offerings go to one chosen place (verse 14). What does verse 15 allow in every town?
chapters.13.summary: A prophet may give a sign that comes true and then urge other gods. Israel must not listen, because the LORD is testing their love. That prophet is to be put to death. If a brother, child, wife, or close friend secretly urges other gods, the same applies. The one who was urged must not hide it. If a town is said to have turned, the report must be checked with care. If it is true, the town is destroyed and burned. Nothing from it may be kept.
chapters.13.lds: Keep this ancient punishment system distinct from present conduct. A sign may come true and still mislead (verses 1–3). What does verse 3 say the LORD is testing?
chapters.14.summary: Israel is the LORD’s children and must not cut themselves for the dead. They may eat cud-chewing animals with split hooves, and fish with fins and scales. Camels, hares, pigs, and many birds are forbidden. Each year they eat a tenth of their crops at the chosen place. If the way is far, they may bring money and buy food there. They must not forget the Levite. Every third year the tithe is stored in their own towns. The Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow come and eat their fill.
chapters.14.lds: Every third year the tithe stays in the town (verse 28). Who eats from it in verse 29?
chapters.15.summary: Every seven years a creditor must cancel what a fellow Israelite owes. If Israel obeys, there will be no poor among them. They must open their hand to a poor brother and lend what he needs. They must not refuse a loan because the year of release is near. They must give freely, because there will always be poor in the land. A Hebrew servant goes free in the seventh year. He must be sent away with gifts from flock, grain, and wine. Firstborn male animals belong to the LORD.
chapters.15.lds: Come, Follow Me studies a willing heart in helping people in need. What “wicked thought” does verse 9 warn a lender against?
chapters.16.summary: Israel keeps the Passover in the month of Abib, at the place the LORD chooses. They eat unleavened bread seven days, the bread of affliction. Seven weeks after harvest begins, they keep the feast of weeks with a free gift. They rejoice with children, servants, Levites, foreigners, the fatherless, and widows. They keep the feast of booths seven days after the harvest is in. Three times a year the men come before the LORD with a gift. Judges in every town must judge fairly and take no bribe. No sacred pole or pillar may stand by the LORD’s altar.
chapters.16.lds: Verse 11 lists who must share the feast’s joy. Who is on the list besides the family?
chapters.17.summary: No animal with a defect may be offered to the LORD. Serving other gods brings death, but only on two or three witnesses. Hard cases go to the priests and the judge at the chosen place. Their verdict must be followed. Israel may one day ask for a king like other nations. He must be an Israelite whom the LORD chooses. He must not collect many horses, wives, or much silver and gold. He must write his own copy of this law and read it all his life.
chapters.17.lds: Which rules stop a king from using his power only for himself (verses 16–17)? What must he read every day (verses 18–19)?
chapters.18.summary: The priests and Levites have no land, and the LORD is their inheritance. They receive set parts of sacrifices and the first of grain, wine, oil, and wool. A Levite from any town may come and serve at the chosen place. Israel must not copy the nations who burn children, tell fortunes, or consult the dead. The LORD will raise up a prophet like Moses from among them. Israel asked for this at Horeb, when they feared God’s voice. A prophet who speaks falsely in God’s name must die. If what a prophet says does not happen, the LORD did not say it.
chapters.18.lds: Come, Follow Me connects the prophet like Moses with Christ. Verse 21 asks how to know a word the LORD did not speak. What test does verse 22 give?
chapters.19.summary: Israel must set apart three cities in the land for anyone who kills by accident. An example is an ax head that flies off and strikes a neighbor. The cities keep the avenger from killing him in hot anger. If the land grows, three more cities are added. A man who kills from hatred is handed over to die. No one may move a neighbor’s boundary stone. A charge needs two or three witnesses, not one. A false witness receives the penalty he meant for the other person.
chapters.19.lds: One witness is not enough for any charge (verse 15). What happens to a witness who lies (verses 18–19)?
chapters.20.summary: Before battle a priest tells the army the LORD fights for them. Officers send home men with a new house, vineyard, or bride. They also send home anyone who is afraid. A distant city must first be offered peace. If it refuses, its men are killed and the rest are taken. Cities of the land itself must be destroyed, to keep Israel from their gods. During a long siege Israel must not cut down fruit trees. Only trees that give no food may be used for siege works.
chapters.20.lds: Read the restraints and the violence together. Keep ancient war law distinct from present religious duty. What reason does verse 19 give for sparing fruit trees?
chapters.21.summary: When a slain body is found and no killer is known, the nearest elders act. They break a heifer’s neck, wash their hands, and ask the LORD’s forgiveness. A soldier who marries a captive woman must first give her a month to mourn. If he later sends her away, he may not sell her. A man with two wives must give the firstborn’s double share to the true firstborn. He may not favor the son of the wife he loves. Parents may bring a stubborn, rebellious son to the elders, and he is stoned. A hanged body must be buried the same day.
chapters.21.lds: Consider whose voice is absent from these laws. Keep the ancient penalties distinct from present family conduct. Why can a father not pass over his firstborn in verses 15–17?
chapters.22.summary: Anyone who finds a neighbor’s stray animal or lost item must return it. A fallen animal must be helped up. A mother bird must be let go when the young are taken. A new house needs a railing around its roof so no one falls. Seeds, plow animals, and cloth types must not be mixed. A husband who falsely accuses his bride is fined, and a guilty bride is stoned. Adultery brings death for both. A woman forced in the open country is not guilty, and only the man dies.
chapters.22.lds: What duties here protect others from harm? The sexual laws reflect ancient rules about marriage and family honor. What must a builder add to a new roof (verse 8)?
chapters.23.summary: Some people may not enter the LORD’s assembly. Ammonites and Moabites are barred, because they refused bread and hired Balaam. Edomites and Egyptians are not to be hated, and their third generation may enter. The army camp must be kept clean, because the LORD walks in it. An escaped servant must not be handed back to his master. He may live where he chooses and must not be oppressed. Israel must not charge a brother interest and must pay its vows. A person may eat in a neighbor’s field but not carry food away.
chapters.23.lds: Keep ancient membership restrictions distinct from present human worth. An escaped servant is not sent back (verse 15). Where may he live, according to verse 16?
chapters.24.summary: A man who divorces his wife gives her a written certificate. If she remarries and is free again, the first husband may not take her back. A newly married man stays home from war for a year. No one may take a millstone as a pledge, because it is a person’s living. A lender waits outside for a pledge and returns a poor man’s cloak by sunset. A hired worker must be paid the same day. Each person dies for his own sin, not a parent’s or child’s. Forgotten sheaves, olives, and grapes are left for foreigners, the fatherless, and widows.
chapters.24.lds: A poor worker must be paid before sunset (verse 15). What reason does the verse give?
chapters.25.summary: Judges must clear the innocent and condemn the guilty. A beating may not go past forty strokes, so the person is not degraded. An ox must not be muzzled while it treads grain. If a man dies without a son, his brother should marry the widow. If the brother refuses, she removes his sandal before the elders. Israel must not keep two sets of weights or measures. Weights and measures must be full and fair. Israel must remember how Amalek attacked the weak at the rear.
chapters.25.lds: Verse 13 forbids a heavy weight and a light one in the same bag. Why does a fair measure matter when a buyer cannot check it?
chapters.26.summary: In the land, each Israelite brings a basket of first fruits to the priest. He says that he has come to the land the LORD swore to give. He says his father was a Syrian near death who went to Egypt. Egypt made them slaves, and the LORD heard their cry and brought them out. Now he brings the first of what the LORD gave. He rejoices with the Levite and the foreigner. In the third year he gives the tithe to the Levite, foreigner, fatherless, and widow. Israel declares the LORD is its God, and the LORD declares Israel his own people.
chapters.26.lds: The farmer brings a basket and tells a story (verses 5–10). Where does the story begin?
chapters.27.summary: After crossing the Jordan, the people must set up large plastered stones. They must write the law on them plainly, on Mount Ebal. They build an altar there of uncut stones. Six tribes stand on Gerizim to bless and six on Ebal for the curse. The Levites call out twelve curses in a loud voice. The curses name secret idols, dishonoring parents, and moving a boundary stone. They name misleading the blind, denying justice to the weak, and secret killing. After each one, all the people answer, “Amen.”
chapters.27.lds: The people answer “Amen” to each curse. What kind of wrong does verse 18 name?
chapters.28.summary: If Israel listens to the LORD, blessings will overtake them. They will be blessed in city and field, in children, crops, and herds. The LORD will send rain, and they will lend and not borrow. If they do not listen, curses will overtake them. They will suffer sickness, drought, defeat, and loss of all they work for. A far nation whose language they do not know will besiege their towns. They will be scattered among the nations and find no rest. They will even be offered as slaves in Egypt, and no one will buy them.
chapters.28.lds: Read the whole warning with care. Avoid using its suffering language to assign blame to someone in distress. What does verse 47 say Israel failed to do in a time of plenty?
chapters.29.summary: Moses gathers all Israel in Moab for a covenant beyond the one at Horeb. He recalls Egypt and forty years when their clothes did not wear out. Everyone stands before the LORD: leaders, men, children, wives, and foreigners. Even the woodcutter and the water carrier are there. The covenant is also made with those not present that day. No one who turns to other gods in secret will be pardoned. Later nations will ask why the land was ruined and hear the reason. Secret things belong to the LORD, and revealed things to Israel and its children.
chapters.29.lds: Come, Follow Me studies inward loyalty and shared covenant identity. Who stands in the covenant assembly in verses 10–11?
chapters.30.summary: When scattered Israel returns to the LORD, he will gather them. He will bring them back from the farthest places. He will change their hearts so they love him and live. The command is not too hard or too far away. It is not in heaven or across the sea. The word is very near, in their mouth and heart. Moses sets life and death, blessing and curse, before them. He tells them to choose life by loving the LORD and holding to him.
chapters.30.lds: The Church lesson compares these words with Lehi’s teaching about agency. The word is “very near to you” (verse 14). What choice does verse 19 set before Israel?
chapters.31.summary: Moses is 120 and tells Israel he will not cross the Jordan. The LORD and Joshua will go before them, so they must be strong. Moses writes the law and gives it to the priests and elders. Every seven years, at the feast of booths, it must be read to everyone. Men, women, children, and foreigners are to hear and learn. The LORD tells Moses the people will turn to other gods after his death. Moses writes a song to stand as a witness against them. The book of the law is placed beside the ark.
chapters.31.lds: Consider how a community can preserve its commitments when a leader changes. Who must hear the law read every seven years (verses 12–13)?
chapters.32.summary: Moses sings a song and calls heaven and earth to listen. He calls God the Rock, whose work is perfect and whose ways are just. God found Israel in a desert and carried it as an eagle does. He fed Israel with honey and oil from the rock. But Israel grew fat, kicked, and left the God who made it. It turned to strange gods, so God hid his face. Yet he will judge his people and have compassion when their strength is gone. The LORD then tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo, see the land, and die there.
chapters.32.lds: The older Church manual connects the rock image with Christ. Israel “grew fat, and kicked” (verse 15). Whom did it forget?
chapters.33.summary: Before he dies, Moses blesses the tribes of Israel. He says the LORD came from Sinai and loves the people. Moses gave them a law as the inheritance of all Jacob. He asks that Reuben live and that the LORD hear Judah. Levi keeps the Urim and Thummim and teaches the law. Benjamin rests in safety, and Joseph’s land is blessed with dew and deep water. Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher each get a saying. Moses ends: no one is like God, and Israel is saved by the LORD.
chapters.33.lds: How do Moses’s blessings compare with Jacob’s blessings in Genesis 49? What does verse 4 say all the tribes share?
chapters.34.summary: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and the LORD shows him the whole land. The LORD says this is the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses may see it but not cross over. Moses dies there in Moab, and no one knows his tomb. He was 120, with clear eyes and full strength. Israel weeps for him thirty days. Joshua is full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses laid hands on him. No prophet like Moses has risen since, whom the LORD knew face to face.
chapters.34.lds: LDS sources teach that Moses was translated. They describe this as a change without ordinary death. What does verse 9 say prepared Joshua to lead?
